text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- HOUSING REFORM DOES NOT EXPAND CREDIT, SAY BANKS

The securitization plan for the so-called FCVS housing fund has not pleased banks as the government expected. Financial institutions say that some measures of the package will have a negative impact on their results and will not expand housing credit.
-- TELEBRAS NETS 2.1 BLN REAIS FROM JANUARY THROUGH AUGUST

Telebras released on Tuesday its preliminary results for the January-to-August period. The holding company had a 2.1 billion real net profit, while the firm's consolidated profit totalled 1.803 billion reais.
-- GOV'T LIKELY TO PAY LESS INTEREST

The federal government celebrated on Tuesday the positive effects of a drop in the Basic Interest Rate of the Central Bank (TBC). The TBC, which was cut to 1.82 percent in October from 1.88 percent in September, will reduce by two billion reais the government's expenses with interest payments.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PITTA HAS 37 PERCENT AND ERUNDINA, 22 PCT

Eight days ahead of the municipal elections, Celso Pitta, from the Brazilian Progressist Party (PPB), who is running for Sao Paulo's mayor office, is steady with 37 percent, according to a Datafolha poll among Sao Paulo voters.
Luiza Erundina, from the Workers Party (PT), rose to 22 percent from 21 percent.
-- TREATY AGAINST NUCLEAR TESTING IS SIGNED
The United States, China, France, Russia and the UK signed an international treaty that bans all nuclear testing. Brazil and 60 other countries also ratified the treaty. India refused to sign.
O GLOBO
-- CEF ASKS MORTGAGE HOLDERS TO RENEGOTIATE CONTRACTS

Federal bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) begins next week to ask 1.4 million mortgage holders to renegotiate their contracts through a program of incentives of refinancing and early retirement of mortgages.
-- FERNANDO HENRIQUE: ONLY AN IGNORANT PERSON WOULD RISK THE REAL FOR REELECTION

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said on Tuesday he would not surrender to pressures or interests which affect economic stability in exchange for the approval of a reelection amendment in Congress.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
